newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields close down on BOK fund supply.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields close down on BOK fund supply.

text.p: Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed lower on Wednesday as the central bank's emergency fund supply to banks improved liquidity, dealers said.
The Bank of Korea supplied 500 billion won.
The overnight call rate rose sharply before settling down towards the close on the central bank's fund supply.
The market will be closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.50 pct vs Tuesday's 12.52 pct
Dealers said three-year yields could fall further in early May after the May 2 expansion in the ceiling on foreign share ownership to 23 percent from the current 20 percent.
The increased ownership ceiling is expected to bring in $500-$600 million during May, dealers said.
They said they expected heavy dollar buying by the central bank to prevent a surge in the value of the local currency and that this would result in ample market liquidity.
